explanation: Compared against erdosproblems.com/652: with R(x_i) = #{|x_j − x_i| : j ≠ i} sorted increasingly, α_k is minimal such that for all large n some n-point set has R(x_k) < α_k √n; is α_k → ∞? AdmissibleConstant k a says a > 0 and eventually some n-point set has at least k points with distinctDistancesFrom < a√n (which is exactly R(x_k) < a√n without fixing an ordering); distinctDistancesFrom counts distances from the point to the others (points.erase pt). alpha k is the infimum of admissible constants, the right reading of 'minimal' for a strict inequality. The statement Tendsto alpha atTop atTop is the 'yes' answer, which follows from Mathialagan's bound as the page notes. Faithful.
